prices_monthly.csv.retrieved_by: Browser fetch of the Yahoo Finance chart API (same endpoint family as Lab 15), run from the Claude desktop app's browser pane on Shrey's computer
prices_monthly.csv.field: indicators.adjclose[0].adjclose (Adj Close: price adjusted for distributions and splits)
prices_monthly.csv.method: Daily bars requested with period1=1167609600 (2007-01-01) and period2=1795200000; for each calendar month the LAST trading day's Adj Close is kept, so each row's date is a real trading day. Rows kept: 2008-06-30 (first month-end with all four funds; VT began trading 2008-06-26) to 2026-10-30 (last complete month on the retrieval date). November 2026 is incomplete and excluded.
prices_monthly.csv.cross_check: The daily-derived month-end Adj Close was compared with Yahoo's own monthly bars for every overlapping month. For every complete month the largest relative gap is below 0.0002% for all four funds. The only larger gaps (up to 1.34% for VT) are in November 2026, a partial month that is excluded from the file.

BIL.name: State Street SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Month T-Bill ETF

LQD.name: iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF

prices_monthly.csv.known_caveat: Yahoo back-adjusts Adj Close every time a fund pays a distribution, so a later download shows different price LEVELS for old months. Monthly RETURNS are what the model uses and they are essentially unchanged by later adjustments. This file is a snapshot as of the retrieval date, not a point-in-time archive of each historical month.

gs2_vintages.csv.source: ALFRED (Archival FRED), Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; series GS2 from the Federal Reserve Board H.15 release
gs2_vintages.csv.method: One request per decision date to alfredgraph.csv with vintage_date = that date; the last non-missing observation in that vintage is what was knowable on the decision date. Each vintage was also compared with the 2026-11-19 vintage: 0 revised values in every vintage.
